newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Dubinin sees regional economic expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees regional economic expansion.

text.p: Russia foresees the expansion of economic activity of individual regions and the development of inter-regional economic ties, Sergei Dubinin, Russia's central bank chairman, said on Tuesday.

Speaking at a conference in London Dubinin said: "The evolving market system in Russia envisages the expansion of economic activity of individual regions and the consolidation and development of inter-regional economic ties within the framework of a single Federative State.
"It is in the regions that the basis of long-term stabilisation of the Russian economy should be strengthened and it must be given all possible assistance at Federal level," Dubinin said.
By the year 2000, foreign investments in Russia are expected to be between $10 billion to $12 billion per year, Dubinin said.

"Over 65 percent of all foreign investments are concentrated in the central economic region, while the overwhelming portion goes to Moscow...the other regions receive a great deal less foreign investments," he said.
